stop: when the tasks are done, or at the end of one session: then stop and report what is left

name: s20-p5-rules: the geometry rules
read: build/reports/s20-plan.md sections 'In short', 4 (P4, P5) and 7; build/reports/s20-p4-boxes.md (the box reader you build on)
build/tools/review/boxes.mjs, build/sandbox/lib/boxes.mjs, boxes-play.mjs; build/tools/review/panelcheck.mjs and pillcheck.mjs (reuse what fits)
owns: a new build/sandbox/lib/geometry.mjs (+ geometry.test.mjs) and its wiring as a --rules option of build/tools/review/boxes.mjs
build/sandbox/lib/boxes.mjs and boxes-play.mjs only where the rules need more boxes read (never changing what the reference holds without saying so)

tasks.do: About ten rules, run on the boxes read at every moment and size: (1) no two things overlap that must not (a card over a face, a pill or a card's words; the side panel, the bottom row and the play area never overlap); (2) everything on screen; (3) no cut or ellipsised text (a word's box wider than its container, or wrapped beyond its allowed lines); (4) a light sits whole round its target; (5) nothing tappable under 48 CSS px; (6) the frame's slots (side panel, bottom row, play area) in the same place in every game at the same size; plus the few more the box data makes cheap (e.g. the order headline one size and at most two lines on a phone). Each rule's message says what, where and by how much.
tasks.accept: `node build/tools/review/boxes.mjs --game <g> --rules` prints pass/fail per rule with the minutes

tasks.do: Prove each rule can fail before it counts: (a) on the planted faults of P4's tool (a box moved 4 px, a card over a face, a cut word, a light off its target); (b) on still-open faults in the fix list: SH-277 (eggs' order headline set three ways, wrapping to three lines at 740x320) and CK-112 (maani's 'maani' label touching the board's top edge at 740x320). Eggs and maani are not on the box reference: read their boxes with a one-off run (no reference written for them). Then (c) every rule passes on chai at L1 and L4 at the four sizes; a chai failure is reported (with picture) for the orchestrator, never loosened to pass.
tasks.accept: a table in the report: rule, the fault it caught, chai pass

tasks.do: Standing: browser runs under your own lock and port (COOK_TEST_PORT=8951, NJG_LOCK=/tmp/njg-browser-8951.lock, flock it); at most --parallel 2 (one other builder may run); commit on your branch often with the two trailer lines (Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> and the Claude-Session line), never push; never change what a child sees; never touch a check outside your new files, a probe, a reference picture or a row's status; keep under 1 GB of runs.
tasks.accept: build/reports/s20-p5-rules.md with a Proof section, under 600 words
